newsitem.title: USA: California rapist-mutilator charged with murder.
newsitem.headline: California rapist-mutilator charged with murder.

text.p: Lawrence Singleton, who was paroled after serving eight years of a 14-year sentence for raping and mutilating a California teenager, appeared in a Tampa court on Friday accused of killing a prostitute.

Singleton, dressed in an orange prison suit for the brief appearance, has been charged by police with first degree murder. No plea was entered in court and he was held in custody without bond, the state attorney's office said.

Singleton gained nationwide notoriety when he was convicted in California of raping a 15-year-old girl and then chopping off her arms in 1978. When he was released on parole, no community in California would take him and he moved to Florida.

He was arrested on Wednesday after police found the nude body of Roxanna Hayes, 31, lying in a pool of blood in his house. Police said Hayes had been stabbed many times. She had 99 arrests on various charges, mostly for prostitution.
An evaluation of Singleton while he was still in a California prison found him to be a paranoid schizophrenic with a strong potential for future violence.
Although he was registered in Florida as a convicted felon, no attempt was made to keep track of his movements, said Lt. David Gee of the Hillsborough County Sheriff's office.
Singleton had no job and few friends in Tampa and supported himself on a small merchant marine pension and handouts from his family, according to local press reports.

After he was arrested on a shoplifting charge on Feb. 1, he went home and tried to kill himself by filling his van with carbon monoxide. But neighbours saved him and he was confined for nine days for psychiatric evaluation.
Florida has a sexual predators notification law, under which neighbours of released convicts must be notified, but it only came into effect in 1994 so did not apply to Singleton.
